title: How to do towel curls
summary: NH demonstrates towel curls, an arm wrestling exercise for wrist and pronation strength, adapted for forearm and biceps hypertrophy. He explains setup with a small grippy towel through a plate, bracing the elbow on the leg, curling up, rotating the wrist inward at the top, a slow negative, and resetting the wrist each rep. He recommends starting light, around 10-15 lbs.

claims.claim: Arm wrestlers tend to have the biggest forearms and biceps of all natural athletes, so he copies their training; bodybuilding is about doing what works.
Use a small, grippy towel; a big towel is cumbersome. Plates with handles make threading easy, otherwise stack small plates.
Grab enough towel to prevent slipping, plant the elbow inside your leg for leverage, curl up, rotate the wrist inward at the top to engage the forearm, and lower slowly.
Reset the wrist each time the weight touches the floor; the reset pull is pure forearm, while the negative is done with the whole arm, the strongest position.
Towel curls reactivate a forearm portion that is his smallest and hit the biceps short head, especially during the top squeeze.
Don't use full range of motion: keep the arm slightly flexed at the bottom to maintain tension, go as high as possible on top and squeeze while rotating the forearm in.
Start towel curls with low weight, about 10-15 lbs, since they are challenging.
